audience.programmeDescription: Scandinavian Languages and Cultures at the University of Amsterdam, presented as Scandinavia Studies, examines the region’s languages, literature, cultural history and contemporary societies. Students specialise in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish and develop receptive knowledge of the other two languages. This example follows Danish and includes study in Copenhagen.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in literature, comparative myth, language processing, cultural interpretation, European institutions, social policy and research methods. These contributions do not form sustained study of Scandinavia’s languages, literatures, cultural histories or contemporary societies across a full programme. The wider combinations become general humanities or European social science rather than a sufficiently close response to Scandinavia Studies.

componentNotes.sca-132110286y: The first year also requires a Dutch writing diagnostic. Tutoring and study guidance continue throughout the programme. These requirements carry no credits.
componentNotes.sca-132111046y: This example uses Danish as the main language. Norwegian and Swedish are alternative main-language choices.
componentNotes.sca-132111066y: Complete Danish 2 before Danish 3. The language sequence also develops knowledge of Danish history, culture and contemporary society.
componentNotes.sca-132110296y: Attend Danish 1–3 before this course. The Vikings course then requires attendance in Danish 1–4 and Modern Scandinavia.
componentNotes.sca-132215026y: Complete the first-year Danish route before this course. It studies nineteenth- to twenty-first-century poetry, fiction and other literary texts in Danish.
componentNotes.sca-132221086y: Pass Danish 4 before Danish 5. This unit also develops reading and listening in Norwegian and Swedish.
componentNotes.sca-132221008y: This example uses Copenhagen, the first Danish destination in the exchange course list. Complete at least 54 first-year EC and attend the first semester of year two before departure. The 30 EC must follow programme subject lines in cultural history, language/translation or literature; Danish, Norwegian and Swedish language-proficiency courses cannot count. A home alternative requires Examination Board approval.
componentNotes.sca-132221126y: Complete the earlier language preparation, including Danish 5 and receptive-language study, and Languages of the North before this research project.
componentNotes.sca-132221036y: Complete Danish 1–5 before translation. The course combines Danish-to-Dutch practice, source-text analysis, translation theory and Danish creative writing.
componentNotes.sca-approved-free-profiling-space: Use this 30 EC for electives, a minor, a placement or approved study abroad. Normally no more than 12 EC may be introductory; an approved UvA minor or same-language sequence can permit up to 24 EC. External study needs Examination Board approval. Placements can occupy at most 12 EC, and minors must not duplicate the required language study.
componentNotes.sca-132229002y: Complete the first year and at least 54 second-year EC before starting the thesis. A January workshop develops the proposal. The thesis is 8,000–10,000 words on a Scandinavian regional, linguistic, literary or cultural topic within available supervisory expertise. It is written in a Scandinavian language if assessed writing proficiency reaches B2/C1 or above; otherwise it is written in Dutch.
